solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Verbally assaulted a bored blue in trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are in disarray, so the three words a bored blue are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shouted abuse at a fed-up, gloomy person who was having a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' signals an anagram of A BORED BLUE, ten letters giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To belabour someone can mean to attack them with words, hence a verbal assault.

clue.text: Guides for topless dealers

indicators.note: without a top, so the first letter of the synonym is removed

parts.note: drug dealers are pushers

explanation.surface: Guidance offered on behalf of bare-chested card dealers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the first letter P from PUSHERS (drug dealers).
explanation.definitionFit: Ushers are people who guide guests to their seats, so they are guides.

clue.text: Produce objective to be held by new genre

indicators.note: one piece is held inside another, so the synonym goes within the rearranged letters
a new version of the word genre has its letters made over

parts.note: an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: Making something whose purpose fits within a fresh artistic category.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' gives ENGER, the anagram, which 'to be held by' wraps around the objective.
explanation.definitionFit: To engender is to bring about or give rise to, a sense of produce.

clue.text: A bit of caution at terms for talk

indicators.note: only a portion of the run of words is taken, so the answer lies inside caution at terms

explanation.surface: A small warning given about the conditions of an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in cautioN AT TERms.
explanation.definitionFit: Natter is informal for idle chatting, a kind of talk.

clue.text: Plausible sort of farmland surrounding good university

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other, so the farmland word encloses the two letters

parts.note: arable land is farmland used for crops

explanation.surface: A believable kind of agricultural estate ringed around a fine college.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arguable can be reasonably maintained, so it is plausible or tenable.

clue.text: Cut the flipping bread rolls!

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: buns are small bread rolls

explanation.surface: An exasperated cook telling someone to slice the wretched rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reverses BUNS. 'Flipping' also reads as a mild British expletive.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to ignore them pointedly, the same as a snub.

clue.text: Crime trends are halved when working

indicators.note: only half the word trends is kept, its first three letters

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
on means working or operating, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A news report that offences have dropped by half during work hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halved' keeps TRE from TRENDS; 'are' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason, betraying one's country, is a serious criminal offence.

clue.text: Dress down and remove a ribbon

definitions.meaning: to scold someone severely, an idiom for a harsh telling-off
literally to rip away a narrow band of material

explanation.surface: Changing into casual clothes and taking off a hair ribbon.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for scolding someone and also literally tears off a narrow strip.

clue.text: RADA, for example, is a friend to millions

parts.note: a crony is a close friend or pal
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: Praise for a drama school as a benefactor to the masses.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA (Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, a London drama school) is a word formed from initials.
explanation.definitionFit: RADA is a word made from initial letters, an example of that kind of abbreviation.

clue.text: Combined team played for vocal expression

parts.note: mixed means combined or blended

indicators.note: the word team is played with, its letters shuffled
vocal points to the sound of a word spoken, so the spelling changes

parts.note: the word for, said aloud

explanation.surface: A mixed side performed in front of a singing contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges TEAM into META, and 'vocal' gives PHOR, sounding like FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed metaphor is an incongruous figure of speech, a kind of expression.

clue.text: A part of Hampton Court reportedly intended to create awe

parts.note: Hampton Court Palace near London is famous for its hedge maze

indicators.note: as it is reported, spoken aloud, so a word with the same sound is used

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A section of a royal palace designed to inspire wonder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns MEANT into MENT. HAMPTON COURT is a Tudor palace by the Thames with a famous maze.
explanation.definitionFit: Awe and amazement both name overwhelming wonder, so they are near synonyms.

clue.text: People keeping the peace fight to remove packaging

parts.note: the UN (United Nations) runs peacekeeping forces
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers fighting to strip off wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbox is to take a product out of its carton or wrapping.

clue.text: There's nothing in the orders for instruments

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: OBEs are Orders of the British Empire, honours given in Britain
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A soldier noting that the commands contain nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour; plural OBES.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboes are woodwind instruments with a double reed.

clue.text: Shoot people running company to achieve target

parts.note: to dart is to shoot or dash quickly
a board of directors runs a company

explanation.surface: Gunning down the directors as a way of hitting one's goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dartboard is the round target darts are thrown at.

clue.text: Woman whose tears led us astray?

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wife who strayed, her weeping having misled us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' signals an anagram of TEARS LED US; the whole clue also hints at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a woman who commits adultery, so the clue's woman fits.

clue.text: One seeking food on behalf of a good queen

parts.note: for means on behalf of
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, a queen

explanation.surface: Someone hunting for provisions for a kindly monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A forager is a person or animal searching out food.

clue.text: Lady Jane's responsibility ill-defined?

definitions.note: a noun phrase for something unclear; the question mark allows the adjective as a loose definition

parts.note: Lady Jane Grey was the nine days' queen of England in 1553
an area is a field of responsibility

explanation.surface: A question about whether a Tudor lady's duties were vaguely drawn.
explanation.walkthrough: LADY JANE GREY was briefly Queen of England in 1553. The definition names a quality, so a question mark softens it.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey area is a matter not clearly defined, so it is something ill-defined.

clue.text: Top do

definitions.meaning: slang for kill, as in to top someone
to carry out or perform a task

explanation.definitionFit: Execute means both to put to death and to carry out a plan.

clue.text: Overwhelmed by the chasm in dire need

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another
something dire is in a dreadful state, so the letters of need are wrecked

parts.note: a gulf is a chasm or abyss

explanation.surface: Someone swamped by a deep abyss when desperately in want.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dire' gives ENED, the anagram, and 'in' sets the chasm word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Engulfed means swallowed up or swamped, the same as overwhelmed.

clue.text: Depressing design and function

indicators.note: to function is to operate, so the letters are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A gloomy verdict on a product's look and usefulness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' signals an anagram of DESIGN AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddening means causing sorrow, so it is depressing.

clue.text: Producer to take legal action within one's right

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another

parts.note: I is one, so one's is I'S
to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: A film producer suing as is his entitlement.
explanation.definitionFit: An issuer puts out or produces something, such as shares or stamps.

clue.text: Volunteers sent to bed, given bread

indicators.note: one piece is sent to follow the other

parts.note: pit is slang for bed
the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Volunteer soldiers sent off to sleep after being given bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent to' places the volunteers after the bed. The TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat, pocketed bread of the Middle East and Greece.

clue.text: Hair preparation produced by Post Office?

parts.note: made means produced

explanation.surface: A hair product manufactured by the postal service, oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomade is a scented ointment applied to style the hair.

clue.text: One graduated by short steps

parts.note: a short is a small strong drink of spirits, such as rum
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A person who graduated in small stages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short steps' looks like one phrase, but 'short' is a drink, a measure of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumba is a dance, a sequence of dance steps.

clue.text: Low temperature is subject to debate

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: A cold spell becoming a talking point.
explanation.definitionFit: A moot point is one open to argument, so moot means debatable.

clue.text: Flooded coastal area halts arms trade

indicators.note: trading means exchanging, so the letters swap places

explanation.surface: A news line that a waterlogged shore stops the arms trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trade' signals an anagram of HALTS ARMS.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltmarsh is coastal land regularly flooded by seawater.

clue.text: Call the compiler from the sound unit

parts.note: to phone someone is to call them
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: Ringing the crossword setter from a recording studio.
explanation.definitionFit: A phoneme is the smallest unit of sound distinguishing words in a language.

clue.text: Employer chasing objective consumer

indicators.note: one piece chases the other, coming after it

parts.note: an end is an objective
a user employs something

explanation.surface: A boss pursuing a goal-minded shopper.
explanation.definitionFit: An end user is the final consumer of a product.
